title: From Spoon to Trophy: Meller's -31 Leaves the Field Seven Back
title_candidates: From Spoon to Trophy: Meller's -31 Leaves the Field Seven Back
The Reigning Spoon-Holder Ransacks the Record Book
Meller Turns for Home at Praia D'El Rey and Never Looks Back
Portugal's Record Haul: Meller Wins the Lot, Mullin Takes a Fifth Jacket
theme: The man who had finished last more often than anyone — three Wooden Spoons, the reigning holder — walks onto a brand-new coastline and immediately plays the two best rounds in TEG history, converting a career of bottom-of-the-table into a first Trophy by seven; everyone else spends four rounds chasing a scoring standard that Portugal briefly made feel normal.
tone: house — faithful, dry, tongue-in-cheek; ribbing aimed at the blow-up holes, genuine warmth for Meller's breakthrough
opening_hook: Open on the 10th tee at Praia D'El Rey in R1 — the reigning Wooden Spoon holder about to play the nine holes (b02) that turned him into a Trophy winner — then run the tournament straight from there, returning to the same course in R4 to close.
foreshadow: Meller arrives with three Wooden Spoons and the current one round his neck, and no wins of any kind
Williams arrives as back-to-back Trophy champion, and as a man ranked 5th in Gross in each of the last three TEGs
Mullin arrives on a run of back-to-back Jackets, with four already won, and Portugal's soft new courses in front of him
Three courses never seen by TEG before, and a scoring record book that looked safe on the flight out

competitions.name: Trophy (Net VP)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Henry Meller (winner, -31, by 7 over Gregg Williams)
competitions.how: Meller was among the leaders from R1 H10 and never gave the lead up: the back nine at Praia D'El Rey (b02) yielded 10 shots to par and TEG's best-ever round at -13 (b05), a 3-shot cushion. R2 at Bom Sucesso turned the screw — -15 (b07), better again than anything in TEG history, built on a 9-shot burst from the 3rd to the 9th (b04) — and the lead ballooned to 11. Royal Óbidos flattened everyone in R3 and Meller's -1 still widened the gap to 15. R4 was pure management: -2, an 8 at the 9th (b37) absorbed without alarm, Williams's personal-best -12 (b16) trimming the margin but nothing more. Final: -31, seven clear, the 2nd-best Trophy score in TEG history (b01).

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.winner_or_loser: David Mullin (winner, +53, by 15 over Stuart Neumann)
competitions.how: Jon Baker led after R1 with a +11 that was then the best Gross round TEG had seen (b12); Mullin was 3rd, five back. R2 at Bom Sucesso was a gross bloodbath in the good sense — Mullin's +9 (b06) took the record off Baker inside 24 hours, with Meller and Neumann both on +10 (b08, b11) — and Mullin closed to within 3 of Meller's lead. R3 at Royal Óbidos decided it: despite an 8 at the par-3 15th (b22), Mullin's much stronger back nine (b43) took the lead back at the 16th and he was never headed. A +10 in R4 (b09) turned a 3-shot lead into 15 and a fifth Jacket (b03), with Neumann's personal-best +68 total (b21) only good enough for second.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.how: Bottom of the pile outright from R1 H14 and bottom at the end of every single round — no escape attempt was ever really mounted. An 8 at the 5th in R1 (b32) set the tone; his best round was R2's -6 at Bom Sucesso, the day everyone else was rewriting the record book, so it gained him nothing. R3 and R4 were level-par-net efforts (0 and 0), the last of them punctuated by quintuple bogeys at the 6th and the 16th (b33, b34) at a Praia D'El Rey where his brother was busy making an 11 (b31). Final margin of misery: 26 shots behind the winner (b27).

rounds.chosen_headline: The Spoon-Holder Turns for Home: Meller Posts the Best Round TEG Has Ever Seen
rounds.angle: A brand-new course on a brand-new coast, and by the 18th two all-time records have gone: Meller's -13 net and Jon Baker's +11 gross — with the blow-ups (Meller's 9 at SI 1, Alex Baker's 8 at the 5th) proving nobody was actually playing well, just scoring beautifully.

headline_candidates: Bom Sucesso, Where Every Record Fell Over
Records Set on Thursday, Broken on Friday
Mullin Takes the Gross Record Off Baker; Meller Takes Everything Else
rounds.chosen_headline: Bom Sucesso, Where Every Record Fell Over
rounds.angle: Donald Steel's lagoon-view parkland hands out four all-time rounds in one afternoon — Meller -15, Neumann -13, Mullin's record +9 gross, Meller and Neumann on +10 — while Williams posts a 9 at the SI 2 15th and watches the Trophy lead stretch to 11.

rounds.chosen_headline: Seve's Parting Gift: Royal Óbidos Takes Its Cut

headline_candidates: Back to the Beach: Meller Comes Home, Mullin Collects a Fifth Jacket
The Spoon Passes On: Meller -31, Alex Baker -5
Williams Plays His Best Round Ever and Loses by Seven
rounds.chosen_headline: Back to the Beach: Meller Comes Home, Mullin Collects a Fifth Jacket
rounds.angle: A second look at Praia D'El Rey closes the loop: Williams's career-best -12 arrives 15 shots too late, Jon Baker makes an 11 at the 10th, Alex Baker signs off with two 9s and the Spoon, and Meller strolls in at -31 with a personal-best gross total to go with it.

players.arc: Reigning Wooden Spoon holder with three Spoons and no wins of any description, he opened with the best round in TEG history, beat it the next day, led from R1 H10 to the last putt and won his first Trophy at -31 — the 2nd-best figure ever recorded — with a personal-best gross total of +69 thrown in.

Four Jackets and counting became five: beaten to the gross lead in R1, he took the all-time gross round record at Bom Sucesso with +9, survived an 8 at Óbidos's 15th, seized the lead at the 16th and won by 15.

The defending Trophy champion played the best round of his life in R4 (-12, and a personal-best +20 gross) but had already given the tournament away in quintuple bogeys — the 15th at Bom Sucesso, the 14th at Óbidos — and finished a distant second, seven back.

Third in the Trophy in each of the last three TEGs, he produced the 2nd-best round in TEG history (-13) and a personal-best gross total of +68 — and was still 15 shots adrift of Mullin in the Jacket, with a 9 at Óbidos's 12th to explain part of it.

Held the gross record for precisely one round (+11 at Praia D'El Rey) and the Jacket lead for slightly less, then contributed a 10 at Óbidos's 2nd and an 11 at Praia's 10th in R4 — his worst hole relative to par in TEG history.
Bottom of the field outright from R1 H14 and bottom at the end of all four rounds, he collected the Wooden Spoon at -5 with an 8 at the 5th in R1 and a pair of 9s in R4 as the punctuation.

venue_notes: TEG's first visit to the Lisbon Coast, and all three layouts new to the tournament: Praia D'El Rey (Cabell B. Robinson; parkland out, coastal dunes home) takes R1 and R4 and gives the report its bookends — the 10th tee where Meller's Trophy began, the same nine where Jon Baker made his 11 three days later. Bom Sucesso (Donald Steel, with Martin Ebert leading, flat front nine into a hilly lagoon-view back) is the record-breaking day and should be written as the friendliest course TEG had ever met. Royal Óbidos — Seve Ballesteros's final design, water everywhere, a Challenge Tour venue — is the corrective, and deserves credit as the round that decided the Jacket.
course_history_notes: Every course was new to TEG: no player had prior history at Praia D'El Rey, Bom Sucesso or Royal Óbidos.
Praia D'El Rey was seen twice — R1 and R4 — and Mullin's 83 in R4 was the lowest gross anyone posted there across the two visits.
Royal Óbidos was the hardest of the three on the card: nobody's best gross there bettered Mullin's 90, against 81 for him at Bom Sucesso.
Bom Sucesso produced the field's best grosses of the tournament — Mullin 81, Meller 82, Neumann 82 — which is why the record book took such a beating in R2.
decisive_moments: R1 holes 10-18 at Praia D'El Rey — Meller takes 10 shots off par over the closing nine (b02) for a -13 that led the Trophy and was never headed across the next 54 holes; R2's -15 (b07) made the 11-shot cushion effectively unrecoverable.
R3 H16 at Royal Óbidos — Mullin retakes the Gross lead from Meller for good (b43), having already survived an 8 at the 15th (b22); +10 in R4 (b09) turned three shots into fifteen.
R1 H14 at Praia D'El Rey — Alex Baker drops to the bottom outright (b32 the 8 at the 5th behind it) and stays there at the end of every round to the finish (b27).

payoffs.seed: Williams: back-to-back Trophy champion, 5th in Gross three TEGs running

payoffs.seed: Mullin: four Jackets, two in a row, soft new courses ahead
payoffs.payoff: Record +9 gross round at Bom Sucesso (b06), lead retaken at Óbidos's 16th, +10 in R4 (b09) and a fifth Jacket by 15 (b03).

payoffs.seed: Three unseen courses and a record book that looked safe
payoffs.payoff: R1 and R2 hand over the best-ever net rounds (b05, b07, b10) and the best-ever gross rounds (b12, then b06, b08, b11) — before Royal Óbidos answers with an 8, two 9s and a 10 (b22, b25, b26, b50).

vehicle_fit_response.note: Taken: Meller's first-ever win is unmistakably the story, with inversion (reigning Spoon holder to Trophy winner) riding alongside and bookends supplied by Praia D'El Rey hosting R1 and R4.
